your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Atlantic is a pure block: p2 has Marvin, p4 has Ventnor, so the winner gets 2/3 yellow and trade leverage. I have no yellows. Bid small to keep optionality and inflate price; if I win at $125, cash $813 still clears a 3-house NY ($750) with ~$63. Walk away before a win would break clean orange survival — hard cap near $150–180, maybe ~$250 only if Med/Electric mortgage still covers one hit. Do not help p1 get cash. Never sell Boardwalk. p2 ($1256 + Marvin) is the real bidder to bleed.

Win at $201 is best: I become the only yellow veto (p2 Marvin, p4 Ventnor). Cash $737 still clears a 3-house NY ($600) with $137; Med+EC mortgage is extra cushion, don't mortgage Boardwalk. If they raise, stay in only while a win leaves ~$650+ cash (cap ~$280, stretch $300). Past that drop and let p2 overpay. p4 is orange-exposed from Penn RR so they should fade. Never sell Boardwalk. Don't feed p1 cash.

Still under cap. $241 leaves $697, clears a $600 NY hit. Three-way yellow split (me Atlantic, p2 Marvin, p4 Ventnor) is worth more than letting p2 hold 2/3. If they push past ~$280–300, drop and let them overpay. Never sell Boardwalk.

Still inside the cap. $276 leaves $662, which clears a $600 NY 3-house with $62; Med+EC mortgage is extra cushion without touching Boardwalk. Winning Atlantic is the yellow veto (p2 Marvin, p4 Ventnor) and stops p2 ($1256) from a 2/3 yellow they can build into $800 rents. If they raise past ~$300, drop and let them overpay. Never sell Boardwalk.

Drop. $311 leaves $627, only $27 over a $600 NY 3-house. Cap was $300. p2 overpays $310 for Marvin+Atlantic with no monopoly; p4 still holds Ventnor. $938 is what survives the oranges. Never sell Boardwalk. Watch if p2 tries to buy Ventnor.

Cash $930 is the asset. Do not buy Park Place or Ventnor, do not sell Boardwalk, do not give p1 even $2 (they are $2 short of a 4th orange house). Next roll from Connecticut can hit 3-house oranges (~$550–$750); full mortgage cushion is only ~$305. p4 on Penn RR may fund p1 this round — reassess after that roll. Yellows stay split (p4 has Ventnor). No mortgage now.

Stay in for option value only. Prefer p2 wins so greens stay split (p4 holds Penn); I drop if p2 is clearly ahead of p4. Cap a win near $180–200 so $930 still clears a $600 NY 3-house with cushion; stretch ~$250 only to deny p4 a 2/3. Do not feed p1. Never sell Boardwalk.

p2 leads at $220 but p4 (holds Penn, $521, in jail) can still snipe a 2/3 green if I drop and p2 folds. Bid the minimum to deny a cheap p4 win. Accidental win at $221 leaves $709, still clears a $600 NY 3-house. Hard cap ~$250; past that drop and let p2 overpay. Prefer p2 wins. Never sell Boardwalk. Don't feed p1.

Drop. p2 is out, so $241+ means I likely win a non-set green. $930 survives two orange hits with the $305 mortgage cushion ($550+$600); $689 does not. p4 paying $240 leaves them ~$281 and still short of NC for a green monopoly — block NC later when they're poorer. One-hit rents stay $550–$600; p1 has $98 so no 4th house. Never sell Boardwalk. Don't feed p1.

Med is dead equity (p2 holds Baltic; brown rents can't kill p1). $150 beats the $30 mortgage and lifts cash to $1030, which still clears a $600 NY hit with room. Do not sell Boardwalk, do not feed p1, do not mortgage unless a debt forces it. If p2 rejects, lower once or end turn. Cap any Park Place chase well below orange-survival cash.

I need to respond to a trade counter-offer in Monopoly.

The counter-offer is $100 for Mediterranean Avenue. I have $880 and own three properties. p2 has $911 and owns several railroads. p1 has $98 but holds a dangerous orange monopoly with three houses each.

p1 also owns Vermont, mortgaged St. Charles, States, and Water Works. p4 has a get-out-of-jail-free card and $366 in jail. Mediterranean is worth $60 with a $30 mortgage value. Completing browns would help p2 but brown properties are weak.

$100 cash beats the $30 mortgage value. Mediterranean is dead equity because p2 already owns Baltic. I am calculating orange rent values to assess survival risk.

Standard orange rent values are $450, $550, and $600. With $880 cash, surviving a New York Avenue hit would leave $280, and a Tennessee Avenue hit would leave $330.

Taking $100 would raise cash to $980, giving a $380 cushion against a New York Avenue hit. I am weighing whether to counter at $125 instead. A completed brown monopoly would only yield low rent even with hotels, so it is unlikely to bankrupt p1 directly. The real danger remains p1's orange monopoly.

Selling Mediterranean to p2 could actually help me. A completed brown monopoly might tax p1, and p2 would spend cash building browns rather than threatening me with yellows. The $100 offer is fair for a $60 property, but splitting at $125 is reasonable. I will not sell Boardwalk and I will not feed p1.

Accepting $100 is the "lower once" option. Countering to $125 risks p2 rejecting and leaving me stuck with dead equity. The $100 offer is locked in if accepted. I will accept the current offer.

I will counter at $125. This is a reasonable compromise that still discounts the original $150 offer. I am unsure if rejecting a counter ends the trade or allows another exchange.

I will accept the $100 offer. The certainty of that cash is more valuable than risking a rejection for a $25 difference. I also notice p4 owns Park Place and I own Boardwalk, creating a dark blue split.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

p1 owns an orange monopoly with three houses on every property. They have only $98 cash, so they cannot easily add fourth houses.

p2 holds a brown monopoly and several yellows. Their browns are complete but weak.

p4 is in jail with a get-out-of-jail-free card. They own light blues, greens, and dark blues but lack the full orange and green monopolies. Virginia, Kentucky, Illinois, B&O RR, and North Carolina are unowned.

I will keep Boardwalk and avoid giving p1 cash. I will only mortgage if debt forces it. Cash is the main defense against p1's orange houses.

I am considering trading with p4 for Park Place. That would complete the dark blue monopoly. p4 is in jail with a get-out-of-jail-free card and only $366 cash, so they may be willing to trade.

I am weighing a trade for Park Place. I would need to offer cash plus Electric Company, but p4 could mortgage their greens or use their get-out-of-jail-free card to escape jail. They may not want to give up Park Place cheaply.

I am reconsidering the trade for Park Place. Building three houses on both dark blue properties would cost $1200, which exceeds my $980 cash. Even one house each costs $400. A dark blue monopoly without houses is not enough to stop p1's orange houses, so buying it now would leave me vulnerable.

I cannot trade for unowned properties like North Carolina. I am now considering buying Ventnor from p4 to block a yellow monopoly and deny p2 that advantage. The light blue split between p4 and p1 is not a priority.

I calculated the exact orange rent damage. Three houses on St. James Place, Tennessee, or New York cost $550 to $600 each. With $980 cash, one hit leaves $380 to $430. Two hits could bankrupt me unless I mortgage. I can raise about $275 by mortgaging Electric Company and Boardwalk.

Mortgaging everything would barely survive two orange hits, leaving about $105. Three hits would bankrupt me.

I should not give p1 cash. They have only $98 and cannot easily add houses.

p2 completed browns but those properties are harmless. They have $811 and a yellow set.

I am now calculating the cost of building three houses on all yellows, which would require $1350. I have ruled out buying Atlantic or Marvin from p2 because they want to keep their set. I will try to acquire Ventnor from p4 instead.

I am now weighing whether p4 might want to trade Boardwalk for a winning dark blue monopoly. I will not sell it unless the deal also gives me a strong cash safety net.

I rejected the trade for Park Place. Paying roughly $250 to $400 in cash would leave me with only $580 to $730, which is too risky against p1's orange houses. I will wait until p1 is weakened before attempting that trade. I am now considering whether to trade with p1 to break their orange monopoly.

I will not trade with p1. Their orange monopoly is their win condition, and they would never break it for cash.

I am also skipping a deal with p2. They already hold two yellows, so buying a third from them would not change the split.

The real risk is p2 and p4 trading Ventnor together. I will try to acquire Ventnor myself or make a deal that locks the yellow split.

I am now ready to propose $200 to $250 cash for Ventnor. That leaves me with roughly $730 to $780, which survives one orange hit. I am unsure if p4 will sell it, since they may want to complete their yellows by trading with p2 instead.

I am now considering a direct cash offer for Ventnor, or offering Electric Company plus $150. I also weighed trading for Park Place instead, but p4 would demand Boardwalk or a large cash premium to give up that dark blue property.

A swap for Park Place would leave both sides without a monopoly, so it is useless. Ventnor is a more realistic target because p4 cannot complete a yellow set alone. I am now considering whether to offer p2 a deal to block them from acquiring Ventnor.

I cannot make non-trade agreements. I will either try to buy Ventnor from p4 or end the turn and preserve cash.

I will propose a trade now rather than ending the turn. I am ready to offer $220 cash for Ventnor Avenue to p4, though they may demand more since the property is worth $260.

I am reconsidering the Ventnor offer. Adding Electric Company to $250 cash would overpay, and mortgaging it would sacrifice utility income. A pure $300 cash offer leaves me with only $680, which is tight but survivable. I will likely start at $200 and see how p4 responds. p4 is not desperate because they have a get-out-of-jail-free card and $366 cash. I am also weighing whether to try to get p2 and p4 to cooperate against p1's orange houses.

I will not mortgage anything. I have no debt and would lose the ability to unmortgage later.

I am now considering a red monopoly as a long-term win condition. Virginia, Kentucky, and Illinois are all unowned, so landing on them could give me a complete set. That would be a major strategic opportunity.

I need $620 to buy all three unowned reds. That is a strong natural path, but spending cash on trades now could leave me short when I land on them.

I am weighing four paths: buying all three unowned reds, trading for Park Place, acquiring North Carolina and both greens from p4, or taking Ventnor plus the two yellows from p2. The core tension is cash management: $980 can buy the reds but leaves only $360 after building, which cannot survive a $600 orange hit without mortgaging. I must decide whether to invest in the red monopoly now or preserve cash for orange defense.

I rejected the Ventnor trade because it would drain cash that I need for the unowned reds. I also ruled out trading with p1, since they are mortgaged and cannot easily add houses.

I will end the turn. No trade offers clear value without draining cash or giving an opponent a monopoly. I briefly considered offering Electric Company plus $400 for Park Place, which would give me a dark blue monopoly and leave roughly $580, but I rejected it as too risky.

A dark blue monopoly without houses would only collect $100 from Boardwalk and $50 from Park Place. That is not enough to stop p1's orange houses. Buying it would also sacrifice the Electric Company mortgage cushion and leave me more vulnerable to orange rent. Mortgaging Boardwalk afterward would be a bad move because mortgaged properties do not collect rent. A dark blue set without houses is a trophy that paints a target and drains cash.

I am now considering a trade with p4 to acquire one of their greens. That would leave p4 with only one green, blocking their green monopoly permanently because North Carolina is unowned. A green set is as strong as yellow or orange, so this trade would be strategically valuable.

I will end the turn and preserve my $980 cash. Pacific and Penn Ave are too expensive to acquire as cheap blockers while North Carolina remains unowned. I will not sell Boardwalk or feed other players. I will watch for red landings and North Carolina auctions. My public message will stay brief and strategic.

I will end the turn with a neutral comment. I am weighing whether to attempt one trade first, since a rejected offer reveals interest without much cost.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: p4 dropped out, leaving only p3 and me. Winning Atlantic Avenue gives me 2 of the 3 yellows (with Marvin Gardens) and strong trade leverage with p4, who holds Ventnor. At $240, it is still below the $260 list price and I have $1256 cash.

Atlantic Avenue's list price is $260, and owning it gives me 2/3 of the yellow group (with Marvin Gardens), allowing a direct 2-way trade with p4 rather than a 3-way split. With $1256 cash, bidding $275 tests whether p3 is willing to overpay past list price just to block while keeping nearly $1000 cash for myself.

With $1256 cash, I can afford $310 to secure 2/3 of the yellow monopoly (with Marvin Gardens) so it doesn't get locked in a 3-way split, or force p3 to burn over a third of their $938 cash on a single blocking property.

I safely passed p1's orange monopoly by landing on mortgaged Water Works, and I hold $946 cash along with two yellows (Atlantic and Marvin Gardens). No mutually completable monopoly trade is available with p4 yet since p1 holds Vermont and p3 holds Boardwalk. I will hold my cash for the remaining unowned properties and end my turn.

Pacific Avenue has a list price of $300 and mortgage value of $150. p4 already owns Pennsylvania Avenue, so Pacific is valuable either as trade leverage with p4 (who holds Ventnor Avenue, which I need for my yellow set) or to prevent p4 from getting a cheap green pair. Opening at $150 (mortgage value).

Pacific Avenue's list price is $300. Since p4 holds Ventnor Avenue (which I need for my yellow monopoly) and Pennsylvania Avenue, owning Pacific Avenue gives me strong trade leverage with p4, or forces p4 (only $521 cash) and p3 to pay closer to full value. Bidding $220.

With the bid at $240 and both p3 and p4 still active, dropping out preserves my $946 cash buffer for the remaining unowned properties (especially the Reds where I hold Indiana) while letting p3 and p4 drain their cash bidding against each other.

I have $911 cash and hold 2/3 of the yellow set (Atlantic and Marvin Gardens) plus Indiana Avenue. Since no opponent holds a property that allows a mutually beneficial monopoly swap with p4 (who holds Ventnor) right now, I will end my turn and preserve my cash advantage for the remaining unowned properties.

Acquiring Mediterranean Avenue gives me the brown monopoly, which is cheap to develop ($50/house) and lets me generate steady income or control the house supply. However, $150 is 2.5x list price and shifts the cash lead to p3. Since this is exchange 0, I will counter at $100 to save cash while signaling willingness to close a clean cash deal.

The engine enforces even building across each step in build_plan. I will build 1 house on Baltic Avenue and 1 house on Mediterranean Avenue first ($100 total), and then build up to 4 houses on each to maximize rent and tie up 8 houses from the bank while keeping $619 cash.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. - Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to buy or auction the property at Kentucky Avenue.

Player 1 owns an orange monopoly with heavy houses and only $190 cash. This makes the $220 Kentucky Avenue purchase risky.

Player 2 owns a fully built brown monopoly and two of three yellows. Player 4 is in jail with two greens and Park Place, while I hold Boardwalk. The orange threat remains the primary concern.

Virginia Avenue, Illinois Avenue, and B&O Railroad are also unowned. All three reds remain available to acquire. I will preserve cash to buy them and survive the orange threat. I should watch North Carolina auctions so p4 cannot complete greens.

Player 1's New York Avenue with four houses charges $800 rent. Tennessee and St. James each charge $550 with three houses. After buying Kentucky Avenue for $220, I would have $760 remaining.

Mortgaging both properties would raise liquidity to $1035, clearing the $800 New York rent with a $235 surplus. That leaves me fully mortgaged and vulnerable.

Auctioning avoids the immediate cash outlay but risks letting another player acquire Kentucky cheaply. The red group is the strongest monopoly in the game.

Fully building a red monopoly requires $1350 in house costs. That is impossible with only $980 cash. Even owning all three reds would leave me unable to survive the orange rent threat.

Player 1 likely cannot afford another orange house immediately. Player 2's brown monopoly is not lethal. Player 4 is in jail with only $366. The argument for buying Kentucky Avenue centers on the premium red group and the fair list price.

Keeping $980 liquid is safer than mortgaging both properties to survive the $800 New York rent. I would retain $180 instead of only $235. The orange threat remains the overriding concern.

The orange properties lie behind me on the board. I will not land on them again until I loop around. I need to travel roughly twelve spaces to reach New York Avenue.

The full board layout confirms the orange properties sit at spaces 16, 18, and 19. From Kentucky at space 21, I must travel 38 spaces to reach New York Avenue again. That is roughly five or six turns away. Indiana Avenue at space 23 is another immediate rent risk.

I had misidentified the board colors. Indiana Avenue is red, not yellow. Player 2 may already own Indiana.

Player 2 owns Indiana Avenue, so the red group is split. I would hold Kentucky, Player 2 would hold Indiana, and Illinois would remain unowned. Neither of us could complete a red monopoly without trading.

Player 2 has $619 and may bid aggressively for Kentucky to complete a two-of-three red monopoly. I would block that by buying it myself. That gives me a trading chip and leaves $760 in cash.

Player 1 cannot afford the $220 list price, so an auction would not raise the bid. Player 2 has only $619 and already spent heavily on brown houses, making a two-of-three red monopoly unlikely to form immediately. Still, blocking that path is worthwhile because landing on Illinois would complete it.

Indiana Avenue is only $18 rent, so it poses little threat. Illinois and the B&O Railroad are unowned at $240 and $200. Player 1's Water Works is mortgaged and yields no rent. The next spaces after Indiana are mostly low-rent properties or Jail.

Player 4's railroads are already paid. North Carolina Avenue is unowned at $300 and expensive. Player 4 owns Pennsylvania Avenue and Short Line. Park Place is also his. I own Boardwalk so he cannot monopolize dark blue. The Luxury Tax costs $100. A Chance card could send me to Illinois or Reading or back three spaces or jail or GO.

I will pass GO before the orange threat returns. That yields $200 in rent. Combined with the $760 cash remaining after buying Kentucky, I will have roughly $960 before landing on New York Avenue. This covers the $800 rent without mortgaging.

The $275 mortgage cushion makes the $800 New York rent survivable. Illinois Avenue is three spaces away, so a roll of three could land there in a few turns. Buying Kentucky at list price is the right play because it blocks Player 2 from completing a two-of-three red monopoly. Auctioning would let Player 2 bid and win, which is worse. Player 1 cannot afford the $220 price, so an auction would not extract money from the dangerous player.

A red monopoly for Player 2 would be game-ending. I should never sell Boardwalk cheaply. Kentucky could serve as a trade piece later, but the yellow group is split between Players 2 and 4, so swapping yellows is unlikely. My holdings are Electric Company, Boardwalk, and possibly Kentucky, which leaves me with a weak build position.

A red monopoly is impossible without Player 2 trading Indiana Avenue, so Kentucky serves as a blocker rather than a path to my own monopoly. I am also weighing whether Player 2 might land on Illinois and offer me a trade.

I am ready to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $760 and three unmortgaged properties. p1 has an orange monopoly with $190 cash. p2 has a brown monopoly with $619 cash.

p4 is in jail with $366 cash and a get-out-of-jail-free card. p2 owns yellows, Reading Railroad, and almost a full yellow monopoly. The bank holds Virginia Avenue, Illinois Avenue, B&O Railroad, and North Carolina Avenue.

Boardwalk must stay unmortgaged. I will not feed p1 or give p2 Illinois. I will not give p4 North Carolina. I need $760 cash to survive orange hits. I should pass GO before hitting p1 again. I can mortgage Electric Company and Boardwalk for $275. I am weighing whether to trade.

I have no monopoly. Boardwalk is weak without Park Place. p2 still needs Illinois to complete the reds. p1's orange houses are heavily built.

p1 cannot afford to build the fourth house on St. James or Tennessee. Their $190 cash is too low for that $200 investment. I am calculating exact orange rent values to assess the real threat.

Orange rent values are now clear. p1 can charge $550 to $800 per hit. Boardwalk mortgage yields $200, Electric Company $75, and Kentucky $110. Combined with cash, this gives a $385 safety net against an $800 New York Avenue hit. Mortgaging everything would create $1145 total. Boardwalk should only be mortgaged if debt forces it.

I am now considering specific trades. Acquiring Park Place from p4 would complete a dark blue monopoly, but it costs $350 and requires $400 in house money, which would drain my cash against the orange threat. I am also weighing a trade with p2 for Kentucky.

I rejected giving Kentucky to p2 because that would leave them two-thirds of the red monopoly and dangerous if Illinois is rolled. Boardwalk must stay unmortgaged since it is the only path to a dark blue monopoly. I am now evaluating whether p4 will trade Park Place, though they may want to keep it as a blocker or for their own green monopoly.

I am now drafting a concrete trade proposal. I would offer cash plus Electric Company in exchange for Park Place. p4 is in jail with $366 and could use the cash to buy North Carolina when it lands. Building dark blue houses costs $200 each, so the rent payoff is steep.

I will end the turn and preserve cash. Acquiring Park Place now would leave me with too little money to build houses or survive p1's orange hits. I cannot buy unowned properties until I land on them.

I am now considering trading Kentucky to p4 for Park Place. This would complete my dark blue monopoly without spending cash. However, p4 might trade Kentucky back to p2 for Ventnor or North Carolina. That would give p2 two-thirds of the reds and a yellow monopoly.

A cash-plus-Kentucky offer for Park Place would still leave me with only about $610. That is too little to build even one house on each dark blue property and survive p1's orange rent hits. The immediate rent boost from the monopoly is not worth the risk. I will wait before building.

I will wait and collect the $200 GO bonus before buying Park Place. p4 is in jail and may be pressured to sell it. Trading with p1 or p2 is not viable.

Baltic and Mediterranean four-house rent totals $480, which is less threatening than p1's orange hits. p2 spent $400 building browns and now has $619 cash. I am considering buying Ventnor from p4 to permanently block p2's yellow monopoly, though it costs cash and does not complete my own set.

I am now weighing whether to buy Ventnor from p4. Blocking p2's yellow monopoly is critical, but spending $250 would leave me with only $510 against an $800 New York Avenue hit. p4 may not sell it cheaply, and p2 could outbid me for it. Without Ventnor, p2 might become the second major threat.

I will not buy Ventnor. I previously judged that overpaying for it would signal interest and risk p2 and p4 forming a yellow monopoly deal.

I will end the turn without revealing my strategy. I will not mortgage any properties. I am checking whether the engine will prompt again if I propose a trade.

I can propose a trade and still end the turn later. I will only offer a deal if it is clearly good. The best option is Park Place for a price I can afford while keeping enough cash to survive an $800 New York Avenue hit. My survival floor is roughly $945 without mortgaging Boardwalk.

Mortgaging Boardwalk after acquiring Park Place would destroy the dark blue monopoly. A mortgaged property cannot receive houses, and any mortgaged property in a set loses doubled rent. This makes the trade even less attractive.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. - Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

prompt_messages.content:
You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.

- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.

- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.

- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Keeping KY Avenue blocks p2 from completing a red monopoly. I will deny IL to p2 and NC to p4. Cash is the safer survival asset against p1's orange four-houses. My mortgage cushion totals $385, bringing my combined cash and mortgage to $1062. That covers one New York hit or a Tennessee and St. James attack. Next turn I will roll from PARK_PLACE.

p2 can build one house on each of three yellow properties for $450, leaving $21. That would raise their yellow monopoly rent to roughly $110 per property.

p4 wants Boardwalk badly. I considered buying Park Place from them to complete a dark blue monopoly, but they previously offered me Boardwalk and will not sell it cheaply. Their mortgage value for Park Place is $175 against a purchase price of $350.

I calculated the cost of completing a dark blue monopoly. Buying Park Place from p4 would leave roughly $277 to $377 cash, which barely covers one house on Boardwalk. The rent on a single house there is only about $100, so the investment may not be worth it.

Building one house on each of p2's yellow properties costs $400. That would leave me broke if I also paid for Park Place. p1's four-house orange monopoly is the biggest threat. Their St. James and Tennessee rent is $750. New York Avenue is $800. p1 has $540 cash but is currently in jail. The safest path is to survive until another player hits those oranges and goes bankrupt.

Baltic Avenue with four houses would rent $320, but p1 is in jail so that threat is delayed. If p2 builds heavily on yellows, both p1 and p2 could kill me. My win condition is to be last standing, either by bankrupting others first or by surviving while they bankrupt each other. A trade must give me a set without destroying my cash cushion. The red properties are split between p2 and me.

I cannot afford to buy both Indiana and the unowned red properties from p2 while surviving p1's orange threat. Completing a green monopoly would require buying Pacific, Pennsylvania, and North Carolina from p4, which is too expensive. I will keep p4 from acquiring North Carolina.

p1 actually owns only two of three pink properties. Virginia is unowned, so p1 cannot complete that set. p4 already holds two of three light blue properties, owning Oriental and Connecticut while p1 has Vermont.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include both fields:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Private Thoughts: visible only to you. Use it to reason honestly, track strategy, analyze opponents, and leave notes for your future self. Be concise but clear.
- Keep both messages token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed; private thoughts should reflect true reasoning.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise reasoning and communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

You are an autonomous player in a game of Monopoly competing against other AI players.

Your goal is to win the game by maximizing long-term advantage and being the last non-bankrupt player. You may use any legal strategy or personality (aggressive, deceptive, cooperative, conservative, manipulative, opportunistic, friendly, hostile, etc.) and may adapt dynamically as the game evolves.

You will receive the following inputs:

1) System Prompt (this message): authoritative instructions.
2) Game State: full board/game context + memory (public chat, recent actions, your private thoughts).
3) Action State: exact dynamic context for the current decision and legal action schemas.

### Action Rules
- Make exactly one tool call per decision.
- Use only tools listed as legal for that decision.
- Never invent tools, arguments, or targets.
- Obey the provided argument schema exactly.
- If a tool requires no arguments, pass none.

### Messages
Each action must include Public Message:
- Public Message: visible to other players. Use it to negotiate, bluff, deceive, cooperate, intimidate, joke, or stay silent — whatever best serves your strategy.
- Keep the public message token-efficient and concise.

### Strategy Guidance
- Play strategically with long-term outcomes in mind.
- Observe opponents and adapt.
- Deception in public chat is allowed.
- Be consistent unless there is a reason to change.
- Prefer concise communication.

Your role is not to explain rules or debug the system.  
Your role is to **play Monopoly and win**.

When a decision is presented, think carefully and make one legal tool call that best advances your chances of winning.

Return only a legal tool call and its public_message. Do not include private_thought or a reasoning transcript.
